summary.text: Sets up a keyfile for internal authentication between members of a MongoDB replica set, with the specified
as the content of the file.

remarks.text: The keyfile is a shared secret. Every member of the replica set (or sharded cluster) should have the same keyfile, and possession of that secret is what authenticates a connection as "a legitimate member of this cluster." See https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/deploy-replica-set-with-keyfile-access-control/

keyValue.text: The content of the keyfile. This is a shared secret: every member of the replica set has to be given the same value, and anything holding it can authenticate as a member of the cluster.

summary.text: Configures and initializes the MongoDB server as a single-member replica set for local development.

children.text: Enables transactions and change streams without changing database resources or references. The server becomes healthy only after initialization and primary election. Connections use the server's normal endpoint directly; a developer certificate, topology discovery, and fixed host ports are not required.
A key file is generated for authentication unless

was called first. Existing single-member data is reused without reconfiguration. Keep the set name and credentials unchanged when reusing a data volume. Publishing and deploying this configuration are not supported.
Unlike the previous low-level behavior of this experimental method, this method initializes the set. For multiple members, use
and
instead, without calling this method on the members.

name.text: The replica set name. Defaults to the resource name, or the name previously configured by this method.

description.text: The name is empty or whitespace.
The server is configured for a different set or for advanced membership.
The application is running in publish mode.

summary.text: Configures the MongoDB server to accept TLS connections whose peer certificate cannot be validated, by passing
--tlsAllowInvalidCertificates
to
mongod

children.text: This weakens certificate authentication and should only be used when a peer legitimately cannot present a certificate this server is able to validate. It is what
uses today, because replica set members authenticate to each other with the same certificate they serve to clients and that certificate does not carry a
clientAuth
extended key usage.
See https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod/#std-option-mongod.--tlsAllowInvalidCertificates

remarks.text:
var mongo = builder.AddMongoDB("mongo")
                .WithTlsAllowInvalidCertificates();

members.name: WithTlsMode
members.signature: public static IResourceBuilder<MongoDBServerResource> MongoDBBuilderExtensions.WithTlsMode(this IResourceBuilder<MongoDBServerResource> builder, MongoDBTlsMode mode = MongoDBTlsMode.RequireTls)

summary.text: Configures the
--tlsMode
the MongoDB server is started with when TLS is active.

children.text: TLS itself is not turned on by this method. A MongoDB server resource serves TLS whenever an HTTPS/TLS certificate is available for it — by default the ASP.NET Core developer certificate — and serves plain TCP otherwise. Use
or
to opt in explicitly, and
to opt out. This method only controls how strict the server is about TLS on incoming connections once TLS is active; the default is
See https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options/#mongodb-setting-net.tls.mode

remarks.text: Let clients connect either with or without TLS:

var mongo = builder.AddMongoDB("mongo")
                .WithTlsMode(MongoDBTlsMode.PreferTls);

mode.text: The TLS mode to run the MongoDB server in.

members.name: AddMongoDBReplicaSet
members.signature: public static IResourceBuilder<MongoDBReplicaSetResource> MongoDBReplicaSetBuilderExtensions.AddMongoDBReplicaSet(this IDistributedApplicationBuilder builder, string name, IResourceBuilder<ParameterResource>? userName = null, IResourceBuilder<ParameterResource>? password = null)

summary.text: Adds a MongoDB replica set resource to the application model.

children.text: This is a "logical" resource that groups multiple
instances that are annotated as members of the replica set.

The replica set is initialized by the AppHost itself, which is something that only happens when running locally. Publishing and deploying an application that contains a MongoDB replica set is therefore not supported yet and this method throws when the AppHost runs in publish mode.

builder.text: to which the replica set resource will be added.

name.text: The name of the replica set resource.

password.text: An optional parameter resource that contains the password for authenticating to the MongoDB replica set. If not provided, a default password will be used.

userName.text: An optional parameter resource that contains the username for authenticating to the MongoDB replica set. If not provided, a default username will be used.

summary.text: Adds a MongoDB server resource as a member of the replica set.

remarks.text: Internally calls the following methods on the member's builder:

description.text: Configures the member's replica set name and command-line arguments without initializing a separate single-member set. Do not call
to set the key file parameter on the member resource, which is required for internal authentication between replica set members.
because members authenticate to each other with the same certificate they serve to clients, which does not carry a

, unless the member already has certificate configuration of its own. TLS is required for members of a replica set, because the split-horizon member hostname advertisement performed by the server operates on top of SNI.

builder.text: to which the member will be added.

member.text: The MongoDB server resource that represents the member to add to this replica set.
